description.value: This study investigates regional coherence between white matter microstructure and gray matter volume and perfusion measures in Alzheimer's disease and behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia using a correlational approach.

spans.text: This study investigates regional coherence between white matter (WM) microstructure and gray matter (GM) volume and perfusion measures in Alzheimer's disease (AD) and behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD) using a correlational approach.

description.value: Observational cross-sectional study of patients with Alzheimer's disease, behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia, and healthy controls.

spans.text: Our cross-sectional correlational study design does not allow for claims on changes over time

Parallel with our findings, in bvFTD, functional connectivity is generally found to be higher in the parietal than in the frontal DMN, whereas in AD functional connectivity is found to be lower in the parietal than in the frontal DMN ( ).

name.value: Positive WM-GM coherence in AD versus controls

definition.value: In AD patients compared with controls, strong positive correlations were found between cingulum WM microstructure and frontal GM perfusion and temporal GM volume, and between inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus WM microstructure and occipital GM volume and perfusion.

spans.text: In AD patients compared with controls, strong positive correlations were found between cingulum WM microstructure and frontal GM perfusion and temporal GM volume, and between inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus WM microstructure and occipital GM volume and perfusion.

value: In AD patients compared with controls, strong positive correlations were found between cingulum WM microstructure and frontal GM perfusion and temporal GM volume, and between inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus WM microstructure and occipital GM volume and perfusion.
This coherence was strongly increased compared with controls in regions implicated in AD pathology and may reflect concurrent degeneration of WM and GM.

name.value: Positive WM-GM coherence in bvFTD versus controls

definition.value: In bvFTD patients compared with controls, strong positive correlations were found between cingulum WM microstructure and parietal GM perfusion and temporal GM volume.

spans.text: In bvFTD patients compared with controls, strong positive correlations were found between cingulum WM microstructure and parietal GM perfusion and temporal GM volume.

value: In bvFTD patients compared with controls, strong positive correlations were found between cingulum WM microstructure and parietal GM perfusion and temporal GM volume.
This coherence was strongly increased compared with controls in regions implicated in bvFTD pathology and may reflect concurrent degeneration of WM and GM.

name.value: Positive WM-GM coherence in bvFTD versus AD

definition.value: In bvFTD compared with AD, a strong positive correlation was observed between cingulum WM microstructure and parietal GM perfusion.

value: In bvFTD compared with AD, a strong positive correlation was observed between cingulum WM microstructure and parietal GM perfusion.
This regional coherence was present in bvFTD but absent in AD.

name.value: Negative WM-GM coherence in bvFTD versus AD

definition.value: Not a stronger, but negative rather than positive correlation was observed between uncinate fasciculus WM microstructure and frontal GM perfusion.

spans.text: Not a stronger, but negative rather than positive correlation was observed between uncinate fasciculus WM microstructure and frontal GM perfusion.

value: In bvFTD compared with AD, a negative rather than positive correlation was observed between uncinate fasciculus WM microstructure and frontal GM perfusion.
The negative coherence may indicate diverging WM and GM changes; slightly increased frontal perfusion in bvFTD may suggest functional compensation for structural damage.
